rounds.text: Evoq Remedies Ltd trades at a steep and unwarranted discount, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.10x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.54x [E1, E6]. This implies the market capitalisation of ₹ 4.50 Cr is severely depressed relative to the underlying book value of ₹ 17.8 per share, leaving the stock sitting at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range [E1, E2, E4]. Beneath this pessimism lies explosive top-line momentum, demonstrated by a compounded sales growth rate of 117% over the trailing twelve months and 21% over 5 years [E13, E15]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -367% alongside a negative return on equity of -0.54% [E8, E16]. Nevertheless, the sheer magnitude of revenue expansion paired with a nominal valuation of ₹ 1.80 per share presents an overlooked asset base where sentiment has entirely decoupled from fundamental scale [E1, E15].

Evoq Remedies Ltd trades at a negative price-to-earnings ratio of -18.2x against a sector benchmark of 19.86x [E5], driven by a devastating -367% contraction in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E16]. This catastrophic earnings collapse directly underpins a negative return on equity of -0.54% that severely trails the sector benchmark of 4.7% [E8]. The market is correctly punishing these fundamental deteriorations, leaving the stock sitting at 0% of its 52-week range [E4] and delivering crushing compounded share price losses of -54% over one year [E18] alongside -49% over three years [E17], while offering a zero percent dividend yield [E3]. Compounding these operational distress signals, the screen flags a severe YoY sales collapse of -100% alongside decelerating earnings growth [E56, E57]. Conceded: the company boasts a very low price-to-book ratio of 0.10x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.54x [E1, E6], and has demonstrated strong historical compounded sales growth over five years at 21% [E13] alongside an impressive 117% surge over the trailing twelve months [E15]. However, this top-line expansion is rendered completely illusory by the staggering profit contraction [E16] and the ominous signal that price growth has recently exceeded profit growth by 313% [E43], proving that lofty market expectations are entirely disconnected from underlying financial reality.

The bear points to a negative P/E of -18.2x [E5], but this metric simply highlights severe mispricing relative to the sector benchmark of 19.86x [E5], opening a deep-value window for patient capital rather than reflecting permanent impairment. While the bear highlights a -367% contraction in trailing profit growth [E16] and negative ROE of -0.54% [E8], these lagging metrics completely ignore the massive operational scaling demonstrated by a 117% surge in trailing twelve-month sales growth alongside a robust 21% compounded 5-year sales growth rate [E13, E15]. Conceded: the stock sits at 0% of its 52-week range with a -54% one-year return [E4, E18] and zero dividend yield [E3], but this extreme despondency creates an asymmetrical entry point at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.10x against a sector benchmark of 1.54x [E1, E6]. Finally, the signal regarding price growth exceeding profit growth by 313% [E43] merely indicates that market expectations are beginning to catch up to the explosive top-line acceleration currently taking place.

Conceded: compounded 5-year sales growth is 21% [E13]. However, the bull's interpretation of a deep-value window enabled by a P/B of 0.10x [E1, E6] ignores the reality that the stock sits entirely at the bottom of its 52-week range (0% of range) alongside a one-year share price collapse of -54% [E4, E18]. While the bull celebrates a 117% surge in trailing twelve-month sales [E15], this top-line acceleration is completely disconnected from profitability, as evidenced by a catastrophic -367% contraction in trailing profit growth and an earnings growth deceleration screen reason [E16, E57]. Furthermore, the claim that negative P/E of -18.2x [E5] and negative ROE of -0.54% [E8] are merely lagging metrics is disproven by the signal that sales dropped -100% YoY [E56]. Finally, the scanX signal engine warning that price growth exceeds profit growth by 313% [E43] indicates unsustainable expectations rather than an asymmetrical entry point.
